organizations.normalization_notes: The 2014 Institute of National Remembrance chapter prints Secret Intelligence Service (SIS). This is a British government assignment, not a civilian private employer or proof of transfer into OSS.

affiliations.role_title: British SIS officer; Madrid liaison for intelligence transmissions
affiliations.date_precision: The cited chapter places this liaison activity before March 1941; no start, end, or OSS transfer date is established.
affiliations.research_notes: The NARA index prints Wilfred A. Dunderdale, Cmdr, British A. A Polish government veterans bulletin independently prints Wilfred A. Dunderdale and SIS officer. A scholarly Institute of National Remembrance chapter identifies Wilfred Dunderdale as SIS contact in Madrid before March 1941. Neither source shows a transfer into OSS; any immediate affiliation remains unresolved.

claims.claim_text: A Wilfred A. Dunderdale matching the indexed British officer is documented as an officer of Britain's Secret Intelligence Service in the period before March 1941; this is not evidence of an immediate transfer from SIS to OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: son collègue du Secret Intelligence Service (SIS) – le capitaine Wilfred Dunderdale
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 2014 historical chapter describes French intelligence messages going to SIS contact Wilfred Dunderdale in Madrid before March 1941. A 2009 Polish government veterans bulletin independently names Wilfred A. Dunderdale as an SIS officer, matching the indexed initial and British-service note.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: uncommon full name, indexed initial A and British officer notation align with the government bulletin's full-name SIS identification and the chapter's wartime SIS role; original OSS Box 204 file unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar/pre-OSS institutional role before March 1941. No source establishes whether, when, or how this British officer entered or liaised with OSS, so immediacy is explicitly withheld.
claims.match_notes: The index prints Cmdr while the French-language chapter calls Dunderdale capitaine; service-rank equivalence is not assumed. The SIS affiliation is a historical pathway claim, not an employer or transfer claim.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA page 127 row 34 prints Wilfred A Dunderdale, Cmdr, British A, Box 204. A Polish government veterans bulletin names Wilfred A. Dunderdale as SIS officer; an independent Institute of National Remembrance chapter places Wilfred Dunderdale in SIS liaison work before March 1941. The Box 204 file remains unreviewed and may reveal whether this was Allied liaison rather than OSS personnel service.
person_updates.next_action: Review NARA Box 204 for role, identity, and any OSS entry/liaison dates; do not call SIS an immediate predecessor until directly established.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The original index image and embedded text both print Allen W Dullles, with three consecutive l letters, page 127 row 5, Box 203; no rank or protected identifier is supplied. Princeton holds papers of Allen W. Dulles with OSS telegrams, but the finding aid does not link those papers to this exact index row. Name similarity alone does not authorize the famous biography or Sullivan & Cromwell employer claim.
